description: Rural Electricity Demand in India (REDI) is a data set deposited in Harvard Dataverse by its authors Shalu Agrawal, Nidhi Bali. Data from the Rural Electricity Demand in India (REDI) survey by SPI-ISEP. The dataset contains detailed information on electricity demand in rural India. The dataset covers 10,000 households and 2,000 rural enterprises across 200 villages in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, and Rajasthan. Coverage: national (IN); the metadata date the deposit to 2019. Formats: PDF. Size stated: 43492. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is CC0-1.0. Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support power-system, energy-planning and grid-operation studies. Related record: the repository-level record data-hdv-repository.
